test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-6) Official paper (Held On: 9 May 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Renu's marks were wrongly entered as 99 in place of 9. Due to this error, the average marks of the class were 2.25 more than the actual average. What is the number of students in the class?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net increase in total marks = 99 − 9 = 90

Increase in class average = 2.25

Number of students = Net increase in total marks ÷ Increase in average

⇒ Number of students = 90 ÷ 2.25 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual marks of Renu = 9

Wrongly entered marks = 99

Increase in average marks of the class = 2.25

 
 Number of Students (N) = Total Error ÷ Avg Increase
 
 
 
 Total Error = 99 − 9 = +90 Marks
 
 
 
• 
 

 
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 +2.25
 +2.25
 . . .
 +2.25

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

Let the total number of students in the class be n and the correct sum of marks of all students be S.

⇒ Correct Average = S ÷ n

⇒ Incorrect Sum of marks = S − 9 + 99 = S + 90

⇒ Incorrect Average = (S + 90) ÷ n = (S ÷ n) + (90 ÷ n)

We know that: Incorrect Average − Correct Average = 2.25

⇒ [(S ÷ n) + (90 ÷ n)] − (S ÷ n) = 2.25

⇒ 90 ÷ n = 2.25

⇒ n = 90 ÷ 2.25

⇒ n = 9000 ÷ 225

⇒ n = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Deviation in Averages

When a value is replaced by a larger value, the net increase is distributed equally among all observations. Thus, Change in Average = Difference in values ÷ Total Number of observations.

Combined Average

If two groups have sizes n₁ and n₂ with averages A₁ and A₂, then the combined average is (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Change due to Addition

If a new observation is added and the average increases, the new value is greater than the initial average. New Value = Old Average + (Total new elements × Increase in Average).
